title: Novum Data - Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on Novum's requirements for a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood: strict VPC-only networking, no public egress, cross-account peering between AWS accounts in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, KMS integration and SOC2 artifacts. Discussed tradeoffs between Dedicated vs Private, latency expectations, data residency, and next steps for network diagram and security paperwork.
next_steps: Maya to send SOC2 + security whitepaper and architecture checklist by 2027-11-30
Schedule follow-up network diagram review with Novum infra team the week of 2027-12-06
Provide pricing estimate for 3-node Dedicated/private pilot and hosted fallback options by 2027-12-02
action_items: Maya Chen: share SOC2 report, architecture checklist, and sample private-endpoint runbook by 2027-11-30
Liam O'Connor: prepare a proposed network AD/peering config and sample security group rules by 2027-12-02
Daniel Park / Sana Malik: send existing VPC CIDR ranges, account IDs, and tentative diagram before 2027-12-04
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-29
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Novum CTO), Sana Malik (Novum Head of Infra), Ethan Ruiz (Novum Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - uh I'll kick us off. today is a quick discovery to understand your networking and security constraints for a private/VPC deployment of Redwood. quick intro?
[00:12] Daniel Park: Yeah hi I'm Daniel, CTO at Novum. we're looking to move some of our inference workloads off public APIs for compliance and cost predictability.
[00:20] Sana Malik: Sana here, head of infra. our main asks are VPC-only access, cross-account peering between our us-east-1 prod and eu-west-1 analytics accounts, and no public internet egress from the inference cluster.
[00:33] Ethan Ruiz: Ethan, security. we'll need KMS integration for keys, audit logs retention for 13 months, and SAML SSO for console access for our operators.
[00:43] Maya Chen: Great. Liam from our solutions team will cover the infra bits — Liam?
[00:48] Liam O'Connor: Hi all, quick note — Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted, dedicated, and private/VPC. For Private we push the control plane into your VPC and/or provide private endpoints with peering, depending on the pattern you want. Quick question, are you thinking private control plane in your VPC or dedicated nodes in our managed VPC with peering?
[01:10] Sana Malik: We're leaning toward private control plane inside our VPCs. Data governance requires full control of the network. We also want the inference traffic to stay within our accounts and regions, ideally.
[01:22] Liam O'Connor: Understood. So there are a couple implementation patterns: 1) deploy Redwood control plane and inference nodes into your VPC (we ship an appliance/container bundle), or 2) we run dedicated nodes in our infra and set up VPC peering or PrivateLink so your services call a private endpoint. Each has tradeoffs for ops ownership and latency.
[01:44] Daniel Park: For us ops ownership is preferred but we have a small infra team. what's the onboarding burden for pattern 1 vs pattern 2?
[01:52] Liam O'Connor: Pattern 1 — more work for you: you run the nodes, we provide manifests, IAM roles, and a installer script; you'll handle node lifecycle, but you get total network and data control. Pattern 2 — lower lift: Redwood manages the nodes, we peer or provide a private VPC endpoint, but you need to trust our managed infra and agree on peering/route tables.
[02:14] Ethan Ruiz: The trust barrier is big for us. We can't have any inference KVs or logs leaving our accounts, ideally. Do you have an option where KMS stays customer-managed and keys never leave?
[02:26] Maya Chen: Yes — we support customer-managed KMS. we can integrate with your AWS KMS/HSM and make sure encryption keys are resident in your account. For the managed pattern we can still use your KMS over a private endpoint so keys never transit public net.
[02:40] [02:40] Sana Malik: follow-up: we run in us-east-1 for prod and eu-west-1 for analytics; need to keep eu data in-region for residency. can Redwood do per-region private deployments?
[02:52] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. We can provision control plane + nodes in multiple regions. note, cross-region data replication is optional; you can pin workloads to region. If you want a single control plane managing multiple regions, we can discuss latency tradeoffs.
[03:07] Daniel Park: On latency — typical LLM inference latency expectations for our use case are P95 under 500ms for short prompts. do you have benchmarks for private deployment?
[03:17] Liam O'Connor: Our published hosted numbers are different than private because of network. For private within an AWS region and colocated nodes, we typically see similar P95s as hosted — for medium models that's 200-350ms depending on batching and model size. we'll share a perf sheet.
[03:33] Ethan Ruiz: can we run a short perf test? like a 1-week pilot with our prompts and a small pod?
[03:38] Maya Chen: Yes that's a common next step. we can provision a 3-node pilot in your VPC or set up a private endpoint to our dedicated cluster and run the same workload. we'll propose both in the follow-up.
[03:49] [03:49] Sana Malik: about network — we require no IGW access from the nodes. everything must flow via our private subnets, allowed egress only to internal endpoints and to the KMS/private endpoint. is that supported?
[04:01] Liam O'Connor: Yep. Nodes can live in private subnets with no internet gateway; for things like image/model downloads there are two options: you host model artifacts in your S3 in the same account and region and we pull via VPC endpoints, or we provide an initial artifact bundle offline.
[04:18] Daniel Park: We prefer S3 artifacts in-account behind VPC endpoints. We'll need docs on the IAM policy and trust relationship.
[04:25] Maya Chen: We'll include sample IAM policies and an architecture checklist in the follow-up package.
[04:30] [04:30] Ethan Ruiz: on audit logs — we need API logs and operator actions to stream to our centralized SIEM in eu-west-1. retention 13 months, tamper-evident preferred.
[04:41] Liam O'Connor: We can forward audit logs to your Kinesis/CloudWatch/Firehose over private endpoints. Tamper-evidence can be achieved by writing signed logs to S3 in your account and enabling object lock/immutability if required.
[04:57] Sana Malik: what's the network path for webhook callbacks or function calls? we have internal services that the models call for tool-calling flows and those must be reachable only via private routing.
[05:08] Liam O'Connor: The runtime can make requests to endpoints inside your VPC — we configure route tables and security groups to permit that. For managed pattern we create a peering link or PrivateLink; for private deployment it's direct inside your VPC so it's simpler.
[05:22] [05:22] Daniel Park: any constraints for CIDR overlaps during peering? we have a lot of legacy ranges in our org accounts.
[05:28] Maya Chen: Good point — peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs. If overlaps exist we can use AWS PrivateLink with interface endpoints or a carrier NAT approach, but PrivateLink is usually simpler.
[05:41] Ethan Ruiz: about SSO, we use Okta with SAML. operator console access must be SSO tied and RBAC enforced.
[05:49] Liam O'Connor: Redwood supports SAML/Okta SSO and SCIM provisioning; RBAC roles can be mapped to your groups. We'll provide a setup doc and typical role mappings.
[05:59] [06:00] Sana Malik: any firewall or security group best practices? we want least privilege for node outbound and for control plane to node management ports.
[06:08] Liam O'Connor: We'll propose default SGs: control plane management on a small set of ports from your admin subnet, nodes only allow inbound from control plane and internal services. We'll include a sample ingress/egress table in the network doc.
[06:22] Daniel Park: are there any specific cloud region constraints for Redwood-managed nodes? for example, we have some legal requirements to keep eu data in eu region — can your managed offering pin to eu-west-1 only?
[06:34] Maya Chen: Yes, we can restrict to specific regions. For our managed nodes we can create a dedicated pool in eu-west-1 and ensure workloads for that account run there.
[06:43] [06:43] Ethan Ruiz: about encryption in transit — we need mTLS between services and the inference runtime. is that supported?
[06:50] Liam O'Connor: Yes, mTLS is supported. We can use your own certificates from ACM or HSM-backed certs; we'll wire it into our control plane to require mutual TLS for API traffic.
[07:01] Sana Malik: what's the rollback story for model rollouts in private? we need canary rollouts and immediate fallback to a previous model if quality drops.
[07:10] Liam O'Connor: Our console supports canary and A/B rollouts, with automatic fallback. The same features are available in private deployments — it's controlled by the orchestration layer. We'll show the rollout UI in the demo.
[07:22] [07:22] Daniel Park: and about cost — curious about unit economics. who manages GPU patching, upgrades, and kernel optimizations in the private control-plane model?
[07:31] Maya Chen: If you self-host (pattern 1), you manage OS/kernel updates and driver patches; Redwood provides guidance and release notes. For managed/dedicated we handle node maintenance as part of the service and we coordinate maintenance windows with you.
[07:47] Ethan Ruiz: any data residency certs — SOC2 or ISO?
[07:52] Maya Chen: We have SOC2 Type II; we'll attach the security whitepaper and SOC2 summary in the follow-up.
[07:59] [07:59] Sana Malik: ok want to quickly sketch the network flow for the private pattern?
[08:04] Liam O'Connor: Sure: user service in your account calls the private Redwood endpoint (either interface endpoint/PrivateLink or local control plane). The inference node pulls artifacts from your S3 VPC endpoint. KMS calls stay in account via VPC endpoints. Audit logs stream to your Firehose. No public IGW required.
[08:25] Daniel Park: sounds good. If we do a pilot, we want the nodes in us-east-1 for prod and a mirrored cluster in eu-west-1 for analytics; no cross region replication for PII data.
[08:37] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include region-specific configs.
[08:41] [08:41] Sana Malik: any gotchas around subnet sizing for KV cache and persistent volumes?
[08:47] Liam O'Connor: For ephemeral inference pods we recommend /24 subnets for a small cluster; EBS volumes for model cache require appropriate IOPS sizing. We'll include guidance and an example Terraform snippet.
[08:59] Ethan Ruiz: can we limit outbound DNS or egress to only approved endpoints?
[09:03] Liam O'Connor: Yes you can enforce egress only to VPC endpoints and internal services via SGs and route tables. We'll provide the exact IP ranges and endpoint DNS names to whitelist.
[09:15] [09:15] Daniel Park: what's the expected time to stand up a pilot? we want something like 3-7 days if possible.
[09:21] Maya Chen: If it's the managed private endpoint pattern, we can stand up a private endpoint and pilot within 48-72 hours once we have network info and ACLs. If you self-host, depends on your infra team's schedule; usually 1-2 weeks.
[09:37] Sana Malik: about legal — will need an MSA addendum for private deployments and a data processing agreement. who handles that?
[09:44] Maya Chen: Our legal ops team will provide standard addenda for Private deals; we'll surface the DPA and any custom clauses during procurement. we'll start with the security pack while legal reviews the DPA.
[09:58] [09:58] Liam O'Connor: quick note about PrivateLink: it avoids CIDR overlap issues but requires interface endpoints in each AZ and costs; peering is cheaper but needs non-overlapping CIDRs.
[10:10] Ethan Ruiz: cost is interesting — show both options in the estimate.
[10:14] Maya Chen: We'll do that.
[10:16] [10:16] Sana Malik: ok final ask — we need to understand the SLA and support model for private deployments.
[10:22] Maya Chen: For Dedicated/Private we offer SLA-backed uptime and a dedicated support channel. specifics depend on contract tier; we'll include the SLA matrix in the follow-up.
[10:34] Daniel Park: great. next steps recap?
[10:37] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) we'll send SOC2/security docs and architecture checklist by 2027-11-30, 2) Liam will draft sample network/peering/PrivateLink configs and SG examples by 2027-12-02, 3) Novum to send VPC CIDRs and account IDs by 2027-12-04, 4) schedule follow-up network diagram review week of 2027-12-06, 5) we'll include pricing for a 3-node pilot in both self-hosted and managed-private patterns by 2027-12-02.
[10:58] Sana Malik: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[11:01] Maya Chen: thanks all, will follow up with the packet and calendar invite.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., 'peer-in' vs peering, 'KV cache' as 'K V cache' in sections). References: security whitepaper link (shared in follow-up), sample Terraform snippets, perf benchmark spreadsheet.
